properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to STL RESOURCES LLC in Grugan Twp, Clinton County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/12/2022 to STL RESOURCES LLC in Grugan Twp, Clinton county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STL RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/12/2022
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 955502
Permit API: 035-21324
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/12/2022
Comments: On May 12, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a follow up inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. This is follow up inspection to a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad. The area where the water was seeping out near the northwest stormwater vault observed on March 3, 2022 was not flowing. The small berm that was built to collect the seep was was dry and any water that is collected in that area is being vacuumed out. Upon arrival at the well pad, STL Resources was vacuuming water out of the northwest stormwater vault. The conductivity of the water that could not be vacuumed out was 2,500 uS/cm. About 18 inches of water was in the southwest stormwater vault. The water was not high enough in this vault to be measured for conductivity due to not being able to reach the water levels with the field water quality meter. STL Resources has back filled and rebuilt the excavated southwest and northwest infiltration berms that were impacted by the spill. DEP screened the water that had pooled up behind the northwest infiltration for conductivity and that resulted in 187 uS/cm. The conductivity of the small amount of water that pooled up behind the southwest infiltration berm was 40 uS/cm. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 21.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 22.1 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 24.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 23.1 uS/cm. Seep 1 had a conductivity of 188 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a conductivity of 196.2 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 59.9 uS/cm. Seep 3 had a conductivity of 44.8 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 133.4 uS/cm. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 25.2 uS/cm. Stream site names have been reorganized by STL Resources consults. The numbers in parentheses at the end of the site names are the original numbers and the number outside the parentheses are the current numbers. During the inspection, STL Resources consultants were collecting soil samples from the well pad in a grid like pattern to delineate the area of the production fluid spill. Two of the holes that remained open had water pooled in them. Test Pit-209 which was about 7 yards to the north of the northwest stormwater vault had water pooled in it. The conductivity of the water in test pit-209 was 2030 uS/cm and soil conductivity was difficult to measure to due the looseness of the soil in the hole. Soil sample 0651-117 was collected from this test pit and will be analyzed for the Bureau of Labs SAC 530. Test Pit 211 which was about 15 yards to the north of 035-21325, had water pooled in it. The conductivity of the water was 3,800 uS/cm and the soil conductivity was 1,180 uS/cm. Soil Sample 0651-118 was collected from this test pit and will be analyzed for the Bureau of Labs SAC 530. DEP spoke with STL Resources Seth Rodriguez and he said that STL Resources is planning to hydroseed the site's earthen infiltration berms and parts of the site that are lacking vegetation. Infiltration berms 1, 2, 5, 6, and 8 appear to be holding water and not infiltrating within 72 hours. The DEP recommend investigating into the functionality of these berms to avoid over topping or berm erosion. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

Permit API: 033-26466
Unconventional: No
County: Clearfield

Comments: The weather was 72Deg. F and sunny at the time of inspection. This is a follow-up inspection to inspection report (4038729) of Stonehaven Energy LLC., Shaffer Nancy Pad, well # 2 on August 26, 2025. There is 1 active, and appears to be abandoned well on this pad. The wellhead leak was suppssed to be repaired and it has not the leak is still the same. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/21/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 953083
Permit API: 117-21997
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Covington Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/21/2022
Comments: The DEP conducted a follow up inspection of Repsol's Twin Ridge 02-185 well site located in Covington Township, Tioga County on 4/21/2022 at 1245 hours. The weather was 46 degrees with an overcast, rain and moderate winds. DEP Environmental Trainee, Brooke Millisock, assisted me during the inspection. There are ten Marcellus wells capable of producing on location. The site has been permanently stabilized through vegetative cover. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed during the inspection. Containment structures are intact and no leaks or other structural deficiencies were identified. Pooled water that was field measured on the pad surface ranged from 200 to 420 ¿s/cm. There was no evidence of spills/releases observed on the pad surface. Post-construction stormwater management controls continue to collect stormwater collected onsite. The stormwater control basins continue to collect stormwater and were both full today. Water was discharging from the basins outflow pipes. Violations against API # 117-21997 cited on 6/24/2019 remain outstanding at this site. No additional violations are cited at this time. We departed the site at 1320 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/20/2019
Violation Code: 78a73(b) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to prevent gas, oil, brine, completion and servicing fluids, and any other fluids or materials from below the casing seat from entering fresh groundwater, and prevent pollution or diminution of fresh groundwater.
Violation ID: 939562
Permit API: 131-20561
Unconventional: Yes
County: Wyoming
Municipality: Meshoppen Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/09/2021
Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72 hr. Stepped Pressure Build Up Tests (SPBUTs) being performed on all (5) wells on the Hunter pad., the Hunter 21HC, 22HC, 23HC, 5H and 6H. These SPBUTs are being performed to assess the recent remedial work, CET (Casing Expansion Tool), deployment performed on all (5) Hunter wells production casing strings. This is the 5th post CET deployment PBUTs being performed on these wells. - All (5) wells on the pad are in production. The (20x13) annuli are capped and set up to vent to atmosphere via Sentry valves. The (13x9) and the (9x5) annuli are set up to vent to a production tank via 2" common vent line. Comments: On 10/18/2023, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Cowden Unit 3H well site for violations cited on 3/24/2023 (SAIR 3528508, Enforcement ID: 415452, CID #370345). I was accompanied by PADEP Tech Services representatives Brian Bailey, Jeff Reidenbaugh and Samantha Kantorczky. The following was observed:Act 9 site ID sign installedThe well site entrance appeared to be maintained.Access Road Culvert #1 appeared open and functioningAccess road Culvert #2 inlet remains partially blocked with stone. The culvert remains constructed without a channel to covey stormwater runoff toward the culvert. Previously the Department requested clarification regarding the area. The Operators 5/19/2023 violation response suggests that the culvert may convey subsurface water. Access Road Culvert #3 inlet remains partially blocked with stone. DEP Technical services staff have looked over the site and have reviewed the file. In discussion with the complainant/ property owner the complainant stated that they are an 18 year resident of the home. According to the complainant , flooding wasnt as issue until the well pad was constructed. The well site was permitted in 2009, and appears to have been constructed toward the end of the 2009. Photos shown by the complainant show significant rainfall events occurring within the photos. However, significant flows were noted at areas where no earth disturbance occurred upgradient. As significant flows were noted elsewhere, no determination can be made utilizing the photos as to any impacts that are occurring from the well pad. The complainants house was noted to have fill elevated around the structure itself. This fill diverts any surface flows away from the house. The complainants stated that he gets feet of water within the residence, and also acknowledges he likely does not have any subsurface drains to drain subsurface flows away from the basement. A review of the plans and this site visit did not provide any information indicating any stormwater control measures were constructed with the construction of the well pad. The Department is requesting Range Resources provide calculations and supporting documents to show compliance with Chapter 102.8 within the next 30-days the Cowden Well site and associated access road. Determination:Violations remain outstanding

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection conducted and INCIDENT inspection of the SWEPI LP - Gee 848 Well Pad located in Middlebury Twp, Tioga Co. on 8/23/2019 @1145 hours in response to notification of a spill. The weather was 68 degrees, cloudy, 64% humidity, winds WNW @9mph. SWEPI personnel were present onsite assisting in cleanup activities. CTS report#344583 states "April Heater of Shell notified Carrie Knapp (O&G) that approx. 5 gallons of produced water spilled from a separator inside the pack and some of it leaked onto the ground. They discovered it around 8:45 this morning and are in the process of cleanup." As of today's inspection, what appears to be a line related to the separator, for the 23H well, washed out causing production fluid and sand to spray inside of the well pack. The fluid flowed out the side entry door, and the rear entry door, impacting pad material below the doorways. Due to size of the impacted pad areas, after hand removal of superficial material had taken place, and the visual assessment of fluid and sand inside the well pack; it is recommended SWEPI re-evaluate the initial estimate of 5 gallons of fluid released. Onsite personnel stated a vac box was scheduled for delivery for additional waste to be excavated. Secondary containment was delivered during the inspection. Onsite personnel were preparing to power wash the inside of the well pack, while a vac truck removed the wash water from the rear entry door. Cleanup activities were ongoing when I departed the site. Violations of the following regulations are cited as Immediately corrected against the 23H well: CSL 402b SWMA 301 25 Pa Code 78a57 I departed the site @1245 hours. On 8/26/2019 Pat Bernethy, SWEPI Env Coordinator reported the revised spill volume is 5-10 gallons and the spill has been fully remediated.

Inspection Date: 1/10/2024
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator of a release of produced fluid to the pad surface on 1/8/24. The operator reported that the release of produced fluid occurred in a path from the frac tank battery to the production tanks on the well pad when a driver who had already off-loaded produced fluid from the production tanks into the frac tanks left the valve open on the truck which allowed an estimated half barrel of residual produced fluid to leak onto the pad surface when he drove back to the production tanks. The site was covered with snow, slush, and puddles of stormwater during this inspection. I met with Kirby Steck of Range upon arriving on location. He showed me the path where a water truck driver released an estimated half barrel of produced fluid. I conducted screening of the fluid on the well pad between the production tanks and the frac tanks. Near the production tanks, in the offloading area, a puddle of fluid was present beneath a water truck that was emptying the production tanks. The electrical conductivity (EC) of the fluid on the puddle was 5.99 mS/cm. Between the production tanks and the frac tanks, the EC readings were below 2 mS/cm. In a puddle near the frac tank battery, the EC was 2.30 mS/cm. A vacuum truck was also on location sucking up fluid from the pad surface. According to Mr. Steck, the plan was to continue sucking up fluid from the well pad that day and the following day, 1/11/24, and to have a crew come on 1/11/24 to begin excavation on the well pad. Mr. Steck said that the estimated volume of the release was changed to half a barrel after speaking with the trucking contractor who said that the truck had already off-loaded the fluid from the truck at the time that the release occurred. The Department recommends continuing to vacuum up the fluid with elevated electrical conductivity on the pad and to excavate the impacted pad material. Violations noted. Violations remain outstanding for previous releases on the pad.

Comments: Rick Hall of EQT called at 1210 and reported an unknown amount of brine was released at the COP Tract 231 Pad A on March 11, 2025 due to a brine dump line failure.I conducted a site inspection on March 11, 2025. EQT representative Zac Subra was onsite and explained that there are 3 dump lines that run to the produced fluids tank farm. These lines are partially above and below ground (picture 2). The far left line in the picture runs from the compressor unit to the produced fluids tank farm. The other two lines run from the GPUs to the produced fluids tank farm. One is a primary main line and the other is a secondary line. According to Mr. Subra, the lease operator alternates the lines during the winter months. The lease operator discovered a leak today coming from the secondary brine line. The leak was discovered where the brine line meets gravel/soil. Standing fluids were observed in the release area with a conductivity reading of >4.00 mS/cm (picture 4). According to Mr. Subra, no fluids remain in the produced fluids tanks.EQT has contacted Tobias Machining and Welding for site remediation. Tobias staff were onsite digging potholes to try and find the buried dump lines and testing those potholes for elevated conductance. Laureen Butters of Penn E and R was onsite conducting the soil screenings. Please note, exposed soils where the release occurred and in the potholes, showed sandy soils.During my inspection several potholes were dug and tested for elevated conductance. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/15/2026 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Brokenstraw Township, Warren county. CSL 307(a) - INDUSTRIAL WASTE DISCHARGES - Industrial waste discharged, directly or indirectly, into Waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit, authorization, or contrary to rules and regulations of the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/15/2026
Violation Code: CSL 307(a) - INDUSTRIAL WASTE DISCHARGES - Industrial waste discharged, directly or indirectly, into Waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit, authorization, or contrary to rules and regulations of the Department.
Violation ID: 8278411
Permit API: 123-45905
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Brokenstraw Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/15/2026
Comments: A discharge of production fluids is evident at the Conklin Lease tank battery. Mature trees at the southwest corner of the secondary containment area are either heavily stressed or dead. A brine tank is buried within the secondary containment area. PVC lines connect the drain valves of the stock tanks in containment to cutout holes in the surface of the brine tank. Evidence of previous fluid releases in the containment area are visible via crude oil staining and sawdust sprinkled over the oil-stained areas. It appears that the PVC lines connected to the two stock tanks in the southernmost end of the containment area have been the most heavily used. At the time of this inspection, the PVC lines are placed inside the cutout holes of the brine tank. However, oil-staining, visible wetness, and sawdust sprinkled around these cutout holes indicate that at one time fluid was allowed to run over the surface of the brine tank and onto the ground within the secondary containment area. Elevated specific conductance in soils in excess of 3,000 uS/cm was observed beneath both of the aforementioned PVC lines.A pool of fluid was present in the southernmost end of the containment area, in what appeared to be a sump. At the time of this inspection, the fluid was observed to have elevated specific conductance exceeding 4,000 uS/cm. Soils at the bottom of the sump also had elevated specific conductance which measured in excess of 11,000 uS/cm. The floor of the secondary containment area above the sump was found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 2,000 uS/cm. A drainage swale is located approximately 30 feet west of the secondary containment area wall. Upslope soil conductivity readings in the swale were observed at 96 uS/cm. Elevated specific conductance in excess of 4,000 uS/cm was observed in soils within the swale directly across from the tank battery. Crude oil staining was also observed in the swale near the tank battery. The swale transitions to an UNT to Irvine Run with defined bed and banks downslope of the tank battery. The water flowing in the UNT was found to have elevated specific conductance exceeding 13,000 uS/cm. Elevated specific conductance of water was observed throughout the stream at the time of this inspection. The specific conductance of water in the stream was observed to drop below 1,000 uS/cm after two confluences with apparently unaffected sources of fresh water at a point approximately 200 feet north of a culvert and the lease road which crosses the UNT. Because the volume of this release exceeds the 1 bbl threshold, the use of either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process is required.It is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners provide the Department with brine disposal receipts for the Conklin lease.

Comments: On May 21, 2025, the Department conducted a Follow Up inspection of Diversified's Diamond 3 plugged well site located in Nicholson Township, Fayette County following IR 3970276 where violations were issued for failure to restore a well within 9 months of plugging it. Accompanying on today's inspection is Diversified representative Heather Empfield and Next Level Energy representative Roger Wagoner.At the time of this inspection the Department observed the well site to be thoroughly seeded and mulched, Mr. Wagoner stated that new top soil and a different seeding mixture was brought in the week prior with hopes of facilitating vegetative growth. The Department observed some new vegetative growth in these areas however it is not yet exhibiting the 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth requirement. Ms. Empfield stated that since the site is not permanently stabilized yet, the silt fence will stay installed until the site meets its vegetative requirement.In terms of the access road, Ms. Empfield let the Department know that what the Department referred to as the joint meter rise station in IR 3970276, which is before the Diamond 3 well site is actually a pig launching station. In IR 3970276, while believing the pig launching station to be the meter station, the Department had recommended the portion of the access road beyond the meter station be restored. At the time of this inspection, Ms. Empfield showed the Department where the joint meter riser station is. The Department observed this meter station to be beyond the Diamond 3 well site and is accessible using the same road that is used to access the Diamond site. The Department also observed that the portion of the access road beyond this meter station, which leads to the Diamond 4 plugged well is restored and exhibiting vegetative growth. Based on the need for the Diamond 3 access road to remain for other oil and gas use, violations shall remain outstanding pending vegetative cover and E and S control removal at the Diamond 3 site.Transmittal of this inspection report is delayed due to an app IT error.

Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023.There is an active discharge of fluid from the Tank Battery of the Lower Reno oil lease that is permitted and operated by Petro Erie Inc.. The earthen dike appears to be lined with a plastic liner. There is a dike drain that is located in the southwest corner of the dike. The valve on the drain pipe is open and fluid is flowing to the ground. The area inside the dike appears to have been impacted by produced fluid from the tanks. A pipeline between two of the poly tanks was actively dripping fluid. Field screening inside the dike were conducted with the soil probe for conductivity, and all readings were above the range of the meter (20,000uS).The discharge from the dike drain flows south across an open area and into a wooded area. There is a visible impact area extending from the dike drain in an irregular pattern approximately 80 yards from the earthen dike and approximately ranging from 6' to 25' in width. Field screening within the impacted area was conducted approximately every 10 yards. Conductivity measurements ranged from 11,000uS to above the range of the meter (20,000uS). Several areas outside of the impacted area were checked with the soil probe and the levels ranged between 60uS to 164uS. An oil sheen is visible within the flowing water and dead vegetation is also observed including several large cherry trees within the impacted area. The amount of discharged fluid is unknown and based upon the observations onsite it appears that the discharge has been occurring for some time.The dike drain was closed by DEP staff at 8:45am to stop the continued discharge of fluid outside of the earthen dike.Water samples were collected at the dike drain outlet (discharge point) and sent to the lab for analysis. The discharge and the potential that the discharge may be impacting the public water supply was discussed with Mr. Rhoades. Mr. Rhoades insisted that he does not discharge his brine and that he could provide disposal documents. It was stated that the dike drain was left open because of forecasted rain. Violations are cited.The Oil and Gas Inspector (OGI) will be conducting a separate well compliance inspection for the well and other wells on the lease.

Violation ID: 993567
Permit API: 047-25052
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/03/2023
Comments: This is a complaint inspection following a report by the operator of a large production water spill at this site on 4/26 at 7:30 am. An initial site visit was performed by WQSS Rob Bechtel. This inspection was performed with Seneca's Jeff Passerello.The initial spill occurred when a cast iron gate valve failed as the operator was pumping production water to a stimulation operation on the E09-U pad. The pump was in operation at 50 barrels per minute. The operator was able to stop the leak eventually. Water spread out across the northern edge of the site, entering a perimeter ditch. It then ran around the edge ditch of the site and eventually entered an infiltration berm on the southwest corner of the location. The operator brought in a pump and was able to collect a significant amount of liquid from this location. The operator's estimate is that 1500+ barrels of produced water was released. The operator has scraped up ~150 tons of material from the surface of the location and staged it on site to remove to the landfill. A pump is placed and the operator is using it to pump water collecting in the berm into tanks on site. Water does not appear to have passed the berm at this time, at least superficially. The operator has brought in ARM Group to do an initial analysis of the site and to take samples for removal to the landfill. Further inspection on this site will be done as necessary as cleanup continues.

Comments: This inspection occurred in response to a phone call made by Jeff Passerrello, of Seneca Resources, on November 21, 2025. Approximately 10 gallons remained in secondary containment, while approximately 20 gallons spilled onto the well pad. The release was contained to approximately a 14'X12' area on the pad. It is requested that a copy of the documentation for disposal be provided to the Department. Given there is no ongoing discharge and the impacted area appears to have been sufficiently remediated, the violations associated with this incident are considered corrected. A future inspection or site visit will be conducted to ensure that the initial remediation efforts were sufficient.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator Swn Production Co Llc

Violation ID 777458
Permit API 115-20254
Unconventional Y
County Susquehanna
Municipality Franklin Twp
Inspection Type Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date 2017-01-27
Comments I traveled to the WR 73- Webster Well Site in response to a complaint of mud being tracked from the SWN Webster access road onto Hawk Road. At the time of my arrival, Jon Sass (DEP-EPS) and I walked along Hawk Road and found that sediment was leaving the well site and flowing down the roadside ditch heading east in said roadside ditch along Hawk Road. Mr. Sassi found that a cross culvert on Hawk Road was carrying the sediment from the north side of the road out to the southern side of the road and depositing it in a stream channel. It appears that the stream channel is the headwaters of DuBois Creek (CWF, MF). The roadside ditch was nearly full of sediment east of the well site. Any water moving through the ditch in this area was heavily sediment laden. I found that the roadside ditch west of the well site was running clear and nearly sediment free aside from the 2’-3’ from the access road where it appeared that some sediment found its way into the ditch. The access road was in poor condition during our visit. No sign of the rock construction entrance was found. The road appeared to consist of soft mud and it was discovered that vehicles were making ruts that appeared 8”-12” deep. I waved down a SWN truck along Hawk Road to notify them of the situation. At this time, I spoke with Keith Heikin (Completions Superintendent SWN) and explained the issues that Mr. Sassi and I found during our investigation. I also requested that he forward this information along to Afton Sterling because I did not have cellphone coverage in that area. Upon return to the office, I spoke to Ms. Sterling and explained what we saw while on site. I requested that SWN take action immediately to cease sediment from entering the waters of the Commonwealth. I suggested that they rework their rock construction entrance and add additional length of rock construction entrance if found necessary for sediment removal. I also suggested that they install an E&S BMP for outlet protection at the interface of their well site and the Hawk Road roadside ditch. I asked Ms. Sterling to follow up, with what we discussed as well as any action taken or planned by SWN, in an email. Violations associated with this inspection have been attached to Permit #115-20254

Inspection Date: 07/31/2020
Comments: The operator called the Department to report a spill that was found the morning of 7/31/2020. Per the operator, a leak of brine occurred from a poly tank or the line leading from the separator to the tank and leaked into containment. It then ran around a freshwater drain pipe that was placed in at construction.The well is an open flowing well that appears to in production, with the valves opened. The well is plumbed to a gas separator and a 50 barrel poly tank within containment. Some stained soil is apparent between the separator and the containment, with elevated conductivity >1mS noted using a Soil EC meter probe. Vegetation within the containment is distressed or dead, indicating brine discharge. Down slope from the containment, vegetation has been killed in a band consistent with discharge from or around the freshwater drain. Conductivity measured ~11 mS near the drain and diminished down slope, with the final reading over 1 mS noted approximately 100 feet from the tank, in a scour location that was likely from a stormwater event. The total volume of brine leaked is likely close to the Operator's estimate of 30-35 gallons, with approximately 5-10 gallons being outside containment.The operator was called back. They said that they would have a contractor on site to dig up impacted soil early next week. Followup inspection will be dome then.

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/08/2024
Comments: On April 8, 2024, inspection conducted on the Tutelo 2 well in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection was conducted in response to a spill that reportedly occurred the day prior to this inspection at 7:00 PM, and was reported to the Department that same evening at approximately 9:00 PM by Penneco representative Marc Jacobs (see attached Spill Report). The Department spoke over the phone with Mr. Jacobs while en route to the well site, who explained that a dry-rotted high-pressure hose connected to the well ruptured and released from 1 to 2 barrels of oil onsite. He subsequently explained that Penneco representatives were working nearby when they heard the hose rupture and were able to initiate a prompt response. Present with the Department during this inspection were Woodard and Curran consultants Matt Kapral and Clayton Hefner. Additional representatives from Penneco and Woodard and Curran were also onsite.This inspection report is part 1 of 2, covering the Department's inspection in response to this incident.The following was observed:The access road to the well site appeared to be stable at the time of inspection, with no observed evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photo 1). This access road is shared with the Tutelo 1 (129-23915) well site. Materials were staged along the access road for installation of CFS (see photo 2). An unnamed stream or tributary was observed approximately 150 feet south of the well site that flows through a culvert underneath the access road. An oil absorbent boom was observed in this location (see photo 3). The Department spoke with Mr. Kapral and Mr. Hefner who explained that seven additional oil absorbent booms were placed across the unnamed stream or tributary downslope of the cross-culvert under the access road. They further explained that a sheen was observed where the first oil absorbent boom was placed upstream from the access road culvert. Peatmoss was spread on impacted areas not yet excavated onsite (see photos 5 and 6). Brush clearing was conducted on the slope east of the well site to remove impacted vegetation and prepare for excavation of impacted soil (see photos 7 and 8). Minor excavation work had been conducted upon arrival to site to contain impacted material, according to onsite representatives (see photos 9 and 18). Additional excavations were conducted while the Department was onsite. Onsite brine tanks appeared to be sound at the time of inspection (see photo 10). A large tarp was laid west of well site for placement of excavated impacted material (see photo 11). Heavy oil staining was observed on the ground around the well head upon arrival to site (see photo 14). It was equipped with a well tag, and the operator's information was posted on the separator (see photos 16 and 17). The aforementioned sheen was observed upstream of the access road culvert, with fluid beading on the wet rocks in this location (see photos 19 and 20). Due to observations made in this location, the Department subsequently collected water samples in this location. While the Department sampled, CFS installations were conducted (see photos 21 and 22). The overall size of the impacted ground area appeared to be approximately 100 feet by 100 feet at the well site, with approximately 100 additional feet of the access road also being impacted. An oil odor was detectable within an approximate 150 foot radius of the well site. Based on observations from this inspection, remediation in accordance with the requirements of Act 2 is recommended. Violations are being issued in response to observations made during this inspection. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending receipt of analytical results from samples collected during this inspection. Please see IR 3742855 for inspection report documenting the Department's collection of aqueous samples from the onsite unnamed stream or tributary.

Report Details
Inspection Client: M4 ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/15/2024
Violation Code: 78a91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under § 3221 of the 2012 Oil & Gas Act, 25 Pa. Code §§ 78a.92—78a.98 or an approved alternate method.
Violation ID: 8187387
Permit API: 105-21699
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Hector Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/15/2024
Comments: At the time of this inspection this well was Status listed as an Abandoned well. This well has the Intermediate (9 5/8") x Production (5 1/2") annulus vented to a poly vent co- mingled with the other two wells on this site. The well head assembly that was accessible above the cellars water and the fittings attached to it along with the cellar area were checked for combustible gas detection with a Altair 5 X Multi Gas Meter calibrated on 05-01-2024. Results of this gas meter screening were 0% LEL ( lower explosion limit) and 0% Methane. The vent line co- mingled with the other two well's on this site that vents into the poly vent was checked for combustible gas detection and the results were 100% LEL and 80% Methane. This well has an Outstanding violation, 78a91(a) for Operator failure to plug an Abandoned well. Donald Supcoe a M4 representative was at this inspection. No new violations noted at this inspection.
